notCovered: optiland's FFT and Huygens MTF take no injected rays. An MTF of optiland's own is on optiland's own pupil grid, reference sphere and frequency axes, so check mtf-vs-optiland-fft sets two methods side by side and holds them to no limit.

A polychromatic curve of optiland's FFT class. It gives the modulus at one wavelength, so a run of several wavelengths has no FFT row in checks mtf-vs-optiland-fft or mtf-vs-optiland-wavefront. The external counterpart in check mtf-vs-optiland-wavefront is this tool's complex sum of optiland's raw wavefronts; its proof on synthetic sums checks the declared weighting and phase convention, not physical spectral fidelity.

optiland's geometric MTF takes no injected rays either. Its rays are an even grid on the stop surface, out to the clip radius; LensVisualizer's are a lattice across the entrance beam; neither is weighted by direction cosine. Check geometric-mtf-vs-optiland sets the two side by side and holds them to no limit: a difference of the two pupil samplings is written down, not explained.

The bins of optiland's geometric MTF. At one wavelength optiland's curve is of landings counted into bins, and a field whose bins move a value by more than its convergence band (0.005 on the axis, 0.01 off it) has no optiland curve. At several wavelengths the sum over optiland's landings is this tool's, without bins, about the axis point of the image plane; LensVisualizer's is about a chief ray's landing.
Dispersion and white-light weighting. Every engine is handed the refractive indices and the wavelength weights LensVisualizer states; no glass catalog and no spectrum is checked against another.
The choice of focus. A best-focus plane is LensVisualizer's own, handed to every engine as a plane; no engine searches for one of its own.
The sizing of the stop. The stop radius, wide open and stopped down, is LensVisualizer's, by its own rule.

Models of vignetting. Each engine clips rays at the apertures it is handed; how an engine's own MTF fills, samples and calibrates a clipped pupil is its method, and a difference that comes of it is written down, not explained.
Zoom and focus positions other than the lens states a run names, and the catalog beyond these suites.
Fields that an engine's own convergence test did not pass. Their figures are shown apart and enter no review band.

supportable: On 508 configurations across four suites, LensVisualizer, optiland and the reference tracer, given identical indices and apertures, trace the same rays within the gates, and the optical path, geometric MTF and wave MTF computed from those rays agree within theirs: worst landing 3.2e-11 mm (gate 1e-8 mm), optical path 9.3e-9 waves (2e-5), geometric MTF 3.5e-10 (1e-7), wave MTF 1.1e-9 (2e-8); the benchmark covers ten wavelengths. LensVisualizer's diffraction MTF is recorded beside two external counterparts, with no preference between them: optiland's FFT MTF, of one wavelength, differs by up to 0.49, a difference classed as one of method; the comparator's OTF of optiland's own wavefront, per wavelength and photopic, differs by up to 0.0078. Configurations at which a known failure of one engine is listed (2, optiland's, where LensVisualizer and the reference tracer agree) are not counted. Dispersion, white-light weighting beyond the stated lines, focus choice, stop sizing, states not named and the catalog beyond these suites are not covered.
z50Attribution: For the Nikkor Z 50 mm f/1.2 wide open at best focus, the tangential difference between optiland's FFT MTF and the other diffraction estimates at the half field, where every sampling settled, is classed as one of method. The outcomes of the other conditions remain as they were classed: wide open at the full field the FFT computes nothing (not computed), and on the design plane its sampling does not settle (not converged); docs/z50f12-investigation.md describes them.
